tldr: Anthropic signs a $5B/yr deal with xAI to access the Colossus supercluster, doubling Claude rate limits and signaling a major compute expansion
Anthropic launches 'dreaming' in Claude Managed Agents — a memory mechanism that reviews past sessions for self-improvement — plus multiagent orchestration and webhooks
Two new adaptive RL training methods (FREIA and APMPO) address the key weakness of static policy optimization in LLM reasoning fine-tuning

Research.title: Free Energy-Driven Reinforcement Learning with Adaptive Advantage Shaping for Unsupervised Reasoning in LLMs
Research.summary: FREIA introduces an unsupervised RL algorithm that dynamically adapts advantage shaping based on the model's evolving reasoning capabilities, avoiding policy misdirection common in static schemes. This is practically relevant for teams building self-improving LLM pipelines without reliance on ground-truth labels. The approach addresses a key bottleneck in unsupervised fine-tuning workflows.
affiliations: The Chinese University of Hong Kong

Research.title: Adapt to Thrive! Adaptive Power-Mean Policy Optimization for Improved LLM Reasoning
Research.summary: APMPO proposes a dynamic policy optimization scheme using power-mean aggregation that adjusts to the model's current reasoning level during RLVR training, outperforming static baselines. For practitioners fine-tuning reasoning models, this offers a more robust training objective than fixed reward weighting. Complements concurrent work like FREIA in addressing non-stationarity in LLM RL training.
affiliations: The Chinese University of Hong Kong

Research.title: ProgramBench: Can Language Models Rebuild Programs from Scratch?
Research.summary: ProgramBench is a new benchmark testing whether LLMs can fully reconstruct programs from high-level descriptions, probing deep code comprehension beyond typical code completion tasks. This is relevant for teams evaluating coding agents or agentic software engineering systems — the benchmark surfaces capability gaps that simpler pass@k metrics miss. Results will help calibrate which models are ready for autonomous software development workflows.

Research.title: vLLM V0 to V1: Correctness Before Corrections in RL
Research.summary: ServiceNow AI documents lessons learned migrating RL training infrastructure from vLLM V0 to V1, emphasizing that correctness in the inference engine must precede any reward-based corrections. The post surfaces practical pitfalls — subtle inference bugs that silently corrupt RL training signals — that are highly relevant for teams running RLVR pipelines at scale. A useful engineering reference for anyone building on vLLM for post-training.

Tools.title: New in Claude Managed Agents: dreaming, outcomes, and multiagent orchestration
Tools.summary: Anthropic is launching 'dreaming' as a research preview — a mechanism that lets Claude agents review past sessions to identify patterns and self-improve over time, effectively extending agent memory. The release also adds multiagent orchestration, outcomes tracking, and webhooks to the Managed Agents API, giving developers building on Claude a more complete agentic infrastructure. These features lower the engineering burden for building persistent, self-improving agent workflows.

Industry News.title: Anthropic-SpaceXAI's 300MW/$5B/yr deal for Colossus I; ARR growth 8000% annualized
Industry News.summary: Anthropic has signed a deal giving it access to xAI's Colossus supercluster at 300MW capacity for roughly $5B/year, immediately doubling API rate limits for Claude users. This is one of the largest compute procurement deals in AI history and significantly narrows Anthropic's infrastructure gap with OpenAI and Google. For developers building on Claude, the rate limit increase is an immediate practical benefit; longer-term it signals Anthropic has the compute to scale frontier models aggressively.

Industry News.title: How David Sacks crashed and burned in the White House
Industry News.summary: The Verge reports that David Sacks's tenure as the Trump administration's AI and crypto czar has ended in dysfunction, with an internal model review process stalled and little policy progress made. For AI product builders, this signals continued regulatory uncertainty from the US federal government on AI governance. The departure leaves the administration's AI policy agenda — including export controls and safety frameworks — in limbo.

Industry News.title: Apple is enforcing an old App Store rule against a new kind of software
Industry News.summary: Apple is applying its existing App Store wrapper/thin-client rules to AI-powered apps that primarily route to external model APIs, potentially blocking or restricting a class of Claude/GPT-based iOS apps. This creates a meaningful distribution risk for AI product builders targeting iOS — especially those whose core value is orchestrating external foundation models rather than on-device computation. Developers should audit their App Store submissions against Apple's evolving interpretation of these rules.
